sentences.zh: 序

translations.literal: Preface.
translations.idiomatic: Preface

sentences.zh: 夫文以化成，惟聖之高義；

translations.literal: As for wen (writing and culture), by it transformation is accomplished; this alone is the lofty principle of the sages;
translations.idiomatic: Writing is what shapes civilization through moral transformation—the supreme teaching of the sages.

sentences.zh: 行而不遠，前史之格言。

translations.literal: If it does not travel far it cannot endure—a maxim the older histories never cease to cite.
translations.idiomatic: What fails to spread far will not last—a truth the histories hammer home again and again.

sentences.zh: 是以溫洛禎圖，綠字元其丕業；

translations.literal: Therefore there were auspicious charts at the Luo, and green characters inaugurated their great enterprise;
translations.idiomatic: Hence the prophetic charts drawn from the Luo and the mystic green script that founded their mighty reign.

sentences.zh: 苑山靈篆，金簡成其帝載。

translations.literal: On Yuan Mountain, spirit seal-script; on golden slips were completed the records of their emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit-seal writing on Mount Yuan, imperial deeds engraved on golden slips—the lore that crowned their rule.

sentences.zh: 既而書契之道聿興，鐘石之文逾廣，移風俗于王化，崇孝敬于人倫，經緯乾坤，彌綸中外，故知文之時義大哉遠矣！

translations.literal: Thereupon the way of writing and signing flourished; script on bells and stones grew ever broader; it shifted customs toward royal transformation and exalted filial reverence within human relations; it ordered heaven and earth and embraced what lies within and beyond—thus one knows how vast and far-reaching is the timely significance of wen!
translations.idiomatic: Then came the full flowering of written records; inscriptions on bells and stones multiplied; literature reshaped folkways under royal civilizing influence and upheld filial duty within the bonds of kin; it structured heaven and earth and spanned all within the realm and beyond—so we see how immense, how enduring, is the meaning of letters in their age.

sentences.zh: 洎姬曆雲季，歌頌滋繁，荀宋之流，導源自遠，總金羈而齊騖，揚玉軑而並馳，言泉會於九流，交律詣於六變。

translations.literal: Down to the closing age of the Zhou calendar, songs and eulogies multiplied; the line of Xun and Song guided the source from afar; bridled alike they raced together, raising jade axles as they galloped side by side; springs of language converged in the nine currents; patterned verse attained the six transformations.
translations.idiomatic: By the twilight of Zhou rule, hymns and praise poetry had grown lush; masters such as Xun Qing and Song Yu carried that tradition from remote antiquity—writers who coursed together like matched teams, whose eloquence poured into every school of thought and whose regulated verse mastered every tonal shift.

sentences.zh: 自時已降，軌躅同趨，西都賈馬，耀靈蛇于掌握，東漢班張，發雕龍於綈槧，俱標稱首，咸推雄伯。

translations.literal: From that time downward their tracks converged; in the Western Capital Jia Yi and Sima Xiangru made the divine serpent glitter in the palm; in Eastern Han Ban Gu and Zhang Heng unleashed the carved dragon on bamboo slips; all were reckoned foremost and alike hailed as champions.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward writers trod the same path: at Chang'an, Jia Yi and Sima Xiangru wielded prose like the luminous serpent in legend; in Later Han, Ban Gu and Zhang Heng carved draconic brilliance onto their drafts—each claimed the summit of renown and won universal acclaim as a literary lord.

sentences.zh: 逮乎當塗基命，文宗鬱起，三祖葉其高韻，七子分其麗則，《翰林》總其菁華，《典論》詳其澡絢，彬蔚之美，競爽當年。

translations.literal: When the Wei house assumed the mandate, literary masters rose in splendor; the Three Ancestors lent their lofty tones, the Seven Masters shared their polished norms; the "Hanlin" gathered their finest blossoms, the Dianlun expounded their polished brilliance—the lush splendor of their style vied in brilliance through those years.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wei inherited Heaven's charge, a galaxy of writers arose: its founding rulers set the pitch of high style, the Seven Masters of Jian'an each refined its grace; the Hanlin anthology distilled their essence, Cao Pi's Dianlun anatomized their craft—never had lettered beauty flourished so fiercely in one generation.

sentences.zh: 獨彼陳王，思風遒舉，備乎典奧，懸諸日月。

translations.literal: Only Prince Chen of that age—his thinking wind rose forcefully; complete in canonical depth, it hangs beside sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: Only Prince Chen set his genius soaring—fully steeped in the canon, a brilliance that stands beside sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 及金行纂極，文雅斯盛，張載擅銘山之美，陸機挺焚研之奇，潘夏連輝，頡頏名輩，並綜采繁縟，杼軸清英，窮廣內之青編，緝平臺之麗曲，嘉聲茂跡，陳諸別傳。

translations.literal: When the Jin house (metal phase) assumed the throne, letters flourished ever more; Zhang Zai excelled in the beauty of mountain inscriptions, Lu Ji displayed the marvel of burning inkstones to polish verse; Pan Yue and Xia Tong shone in succession, neck-and-neck with celebrated peers; together they wove lush ornament and spun pure brilliance, exhausting the blue-bound archives within the palace and compiling the lovely songs of the Ping Terrace—their fair reputations and splendid deeds are recorded in other biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jin took the mandate, literature bloomed: Zhang Zai memorialized mountains with unmatched grace; Lu Ji wrung marvels from inkstones half consumed by flame; Pan Yue and Xia Tong matched radiance with the greatest names of their day; each lavishly embroidered yet kept the shuttle bright, mining the imperial stacks for lore and weaving Ping Terrace songs—their fuller stories appear in separate traditions.

sentences.zh: 至於吉甫、太沖，江右之才傑；

translations.literal: As for Jifu (Ying Zhen) and Taichong (Zuo Si)—outstanding talents of Jiangyou;
translations.idiomatic: Consider Ying Zhen (Jifu) and Zuo Si (Taichong)—stars among the writers south of the river;

sentences.zh: 曹毗、庾闡，中興之時秀。

translations.literal: Cao Pi and Yu Chan—the timely elite of the Restoration.
translations.idiomatic: and Cao Pi together with Yu Chan—the finest Eastern Jin had to offer at its revival.

sentences.zh: 信乃金相玉潤，林薈川沖，埒美前修，垂裕來葉。

translations.literal: Truly they were gold in appearance and jade in luster, forest gathered and stream deep—rivaling the excellence of earlier masters and laying up blessings for later generations.
translations.idiomatic: They truly combined bronze resonance with polished jade—learning broad as a grove, depth like a river—matching the old masters and leaving an inheritance for ages to come.

sentences.zh: 今撰其鴻筆之彥，著之《文苑》云。

translations.literal: Now I compile those eminent exemplars of the great brush and present them in this "Garden of Letters."
translations.idiomatic: Here we gather the foremost wielders of the brush and set them down under the heading "Literary Garden."

sentences.zh: 應貞

translations.literal: Ying Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Zhen

sentences.zh: 應貞，字吉甫，汝南南頓人，魏侍中璩之子也。

translations.literal: Ying Zhen, style Jifu, was a man of Nandun in Runan, son of Wei Palace Attendant Ying Qu.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Zhen, courtesy name Jifu, came from Nandun in Runan and was the son of Ying Qu, Palace Attendant of Wei.

sentences.zh: 自漢至魏，世以文章顯，軒冕相襲，為郡盛族。

translations.literal: From Han down to Wei, generation after generation they showed distinction in letters; high caps and carriage canopies succeeded one another—they were a great clan of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: For generations from Han through Wei the family had risen on literary talent; rank followed rank until they stood among the commandery's greatest houses.

sentences.zh: 貞善談論，以才學稱。

translations.literal: Zhen was skilled in discourse and was famed for talent and learning.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Zhen excelled at debate and was celebrated for his erudition.

sentences.zh: 夏侯玄有盛名，貞詣玄，玄甚重之。

translations.literal: Xiahou Xuan had a great reputation; Zhen visited Xuan, and Xuan thought very highly of him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Xuan's fame was immense; when Ying Zhen called on him, Xuan treated him with marked respect.

sentences.zh: 舉高第，頻曆顯位。

translations.literal: He was nominated in the highest grade and repeatedly passed through eminent offices.
translations.idiomatic: He ranked at the top of his cohort and rose through a series of prominent posts.

sentences.zh: 武帝為撫軍大將軍，以為參軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu was General Who Guards the Army, he appointed him Army Adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Wu still held the title General Who Guards the Army, he named Ying Zhen army adjutant.

sentences.zh: 及踐阼，遷給事中。

translations.literal: When [Wu] ascended the throne, [Zhen] was promoted to Palace Attendant Within the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne, Ying Zhen became a palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 帝于華林園宴射，貞賦詩最美。

translations.literal: When the emperor feasted and shot at Hualin Garden, Zhen's poem was the finest.
translations.idiomatic: During an archery banquet at Hualin Garden, Ying Zhen's poem outshone every other.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：

translations.literal: His words said:
translations.idiomatic: The poem ran:

sentences.zh: 初置太子中庶子官，貞與護軍長史孔恂俱為之。

translations.literal: When the office of Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent was first created, Zhen and Army-Guards Chief Clerk Kong Xun were both appointed to it.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince's junior mentorate was first established, Ying Zhen and Kong Xun, chief clerk of the Army Guard, were the first to hold the post.

sentences.zh: 後遷散騎常侍，以儒學與太尉荀顗撰定新禮，未施行。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary; on the basis of ru learning he together with Grand Commandant Xun Yi compiled the new ritual code, but it was not put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: He later became a cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and, as a Confucian scholar, helped Grand Commandant Xun Yi draft a new ritual code that never came into force.

sentences.zh: 卒，文集行於世。

translations.literal: He died; his collected works circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He died, leaving a literary collection that circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 弟純。

translations.literal: Younger brother Chun.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Ying Chun:

sentences.zh: 純子紹，永嘉中，至黃門郎，為東海王越所害。

translations.literal: Chun's son Shao, in the Yongjia era, reached the post of Palace Attendant of the Yellow Gates and was killed by the Prince of Donghai, Sima Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Chun's son Ying Shao rose to palace attendant under the Yellow Gates in the Yongjia years and was put to death by Sima Yue, the Prince of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 純弟秀，秀子詹，自有傳。

translations.literal: Chun's younger brother Xiu; Xiu's son Zhan—each has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Chun's brother Ying Xiu and Xiu's son Ying Zhan are biographed elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 成公綏

translations.literal: Cheng Gongshui.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Gongshui

sentences.zh: 成公綏，字子安，東郡白馬人也。

translations.literal: Cheng Gongshui, style Zi'an, was a man of Baima in Dong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Gongshui, courtesy name Zi'an, came from Baima in Dong commandery.

sentences.zh: 幼而聰敏，博涉經傳。

translations.literal: In youth he was quick and perceptive, and he read widely in the classics and commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: He was precocious and devoured the classics and their exegesis.

sentences.zh: 性寡欲，不營資產，家貧歲饑，常晏如也。

translations.literal: By nature he had few desires and did not pursue property; his household was poor and the harvest failed year after year, yet he was always serene.
translations.idiomatic: Content with little, he acquired no lands or fortune; even when famine gnawed his household he remained untroubled.

sentences.zh: 少有俊才，詞賦甚麗，閑默自守，不求聞達。

translations.literal: In youth he had outstanding talent; his ci and fu were very beautiful; quietly he kept to himself and sought neither fame nor advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Gifted from youth, he wrote rhapsodies of striking polish yet lived in quiet retirement, courting neither renown nor office.

sentences.zh: 時有孝烏，每集其廬舍，綏謂有反哺之德，以為祥禽，乃作賦美之，文多不載。

translations.literal: At that time there was a filial crow that always roosted on his cottage; Sui said it had the virtue of bringing food back to its parents, deemed it an auspicious bird, and composed a fu praising it—the text is mostly not recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: A crow famed for filial devotion nested habitually on his roof; Cheng judged it an auspicious creature embodying the virtue of feeding one's parents in old age and wrote a rhapsody in its praise (most of which is omitted here).

sentences.zh: 又以「賦者貴能分賦物理，敷演無方，天地之盛，可以致思矣。

translations.literal: He also said, "In fu pieces one prizes the ability to analyze the categories of things and unfold principles without fixed pattern; the fullness of heaven and earth may thereby be brought within contemplation.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that "a true fu must dissect the nature of things and expound principle without rigid formula—the grandeur of heaven and earth becomes thinkable through such writing.

sentences.zh: 曆觀古人未之有賦，豈獨以至麗無文，難以辭贊；

translations.literal: Surveying the ancients, none had composed a fu on it—is it only because its supreme beauty lacked patterned wording and was hard to praise in phrases?
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity no one had attempted such a piece—perhaps because beauty too overwhelming defies eloquence;

sentences.zh: 不然，何其闕哉？

translations.literal: If not, why was it lacking?
translations.idiomatic: or else why should the tradition have stayed silent?

sentences.zh: 」遂為《天地賦》曰：

translations.literal: " Thereupon he composed the "Fu on Heaven and Earth," which says:
translations.idiomatic: " With that he composed his "Rhapsody on Heaven and Earth," opening:

sentences.zh: 綏雅好音律，嘗當暑承風而嘯，泠然成曲，因為《嘯賦》曰：

translations.literal: Sui was fond of pitch and temperament; once in summer heat he faced the wind and whistled; cool and clear it formed a melody—thereupon he composed the "Fu on Whistling," which says:
translations.idiomatic: Cheng loved musical theory; one sweltering day he whistled into the breeze until pure tones shaped themselves into melody—and thus arose his "Rhapsody on Whistling," which begins:

sentences.zh: 張華雅重綏，每見其文，歎伏以為絕倫，薦之太常，徵為博士。

translations.literal: Zhang Hua deeply esteemed Sui; whenever he saw his writings he sighed and submitted, deeming them without peer—he recommended him to the Chamberlain for Ceremonials, who summoned him as erudite.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua admired him deeply; each essay left Zhang convinced no one could rival Cheng, so he nominated him to the Chamberlain for Ceremonials, who appointed him court erudite.

sentences.zh: 曆秘書郎，轉丞，遷中書郎。

translations.literal: He passed through Palace Secretary, transferred to assistant director, and was promoted to Gentleman of the Palace Writers.
translations.idiomatic: He served as palace secretary, moved up to assistant director, then advanced to gentleman of the palace writers.

sentences.zh: 每與華受詔並為詩賦，又與賈充等參定法律。

translations.literal: Whenever he received edicts together with Hua they jointly composed shi and fu; he also joined Jia Chong and others in revising the statutes.
translations.idiomatic: He often drafted verse and rhapsodies alongside Zhang Hua by imperial order and helped Jia Chong and colleagues codify the law.

sentences.zh: 卒，年四十三，所著詩賦雜筆十餘卷行於世。

translations.literal: He died at age forty-three; his writings—shi, fu, and miscellaneous brush-notes in more than ten fascicles—circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty-three; over ten fascicles of poetry, rhapsodies, and assorted prose circulated after him.

sentences.zh: 左思

translations.literal: Zuo Si.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Si

sentences.zh: 左思，字太沖，齊國臨淄人也。

translations.literal: Zuo Si, style Taichong, was a man of Linzi in the kingdom of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Si, courtesy name Taichong, hailed from Linzi in the old kingdom of Qi.

sentences.zh: 其先齊之公族有左右公子，因為氏焉。

translations.literal: His ancestors were among the ducal kin of Qi; there were Left and Right Young Lords, and from this they took their surname.
translations.idiomatic: The clan descended from Qi nobility—the ancient titles "Left and Right Young Lord" supplied their surname.

sentences.zh: 家世儒學。

translations.literal: For generations the household practiced ru learning.
translations.idiomatic: For generations the family had pursued Confucian scholarship.

sentences.zh: 父雍，起小吏，以能擢授殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: His father Yong rose from petty clerk and by ability was promoted and appointed Palace Assistant Imperial Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zuo Yong began as a petty clerk and won promotion on merit to palace assistant censor.

sentences.zh: 思小學鐘、胡書及鼓琴，並不成。

translations.literal: Si in youth studied Zhong and Hu calligraphy and playing the zither—none succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Zuo studied calligraphy after Zhong Yao and Hu Zhao and took up the zither—he mastered neither.

sentences.zh: 雍謂友人曰：「思所曉解，不及我少時。

translations.literal: Yong said to a friend, "What Si understands does not match me in my youth.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Yong told a friend, "The boy grasps less than I did at his age.

sentences.zh: 」思遂感激勤學，兼善陰陽之術。

translations.literal: " Si thereupon was stirred and studied diligently; he also became adept in yin-yang arts.
translations.idiomatic: " Stung by those words, Zuo threw himself into study and learned the yin-yang traditions besides.

sentences.zh: 貌寢，口訥，而辭藻壯麗。

translations.literal: His appearance was homely, his speech halting, yet his phrasing was magnificent.
translations.idiomatic: Plain of face and slow of tongue, he nevertheless wrote with towering brilliance.

sentences.zh: 不好交遊，惟以閒居為事。

translations.literal: He did not enjoy socializing; he took only quiet retirement as his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: He avoided society and preferred the quiet of home.

sentences.zh: 造《齊都賦》，一年乃成。

translations.literal: He composed the "Fu on the Qi Capital"; one year then it was finished.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted a "Rhapsody on the Qi Capital" that took a year to complete.

sentences.zh: 復欲賦三都，會妹芬入宮，移家京師，乃詣著作郎張載，訪岷邛之事。

translations.literal: He again wished to compose a fu on the three capitals; it happened that his younger sister Fen entered the palace, and he moved the household to the capital—thereupon he visited Editorial Director Zhang Zai and inquired into affairs of Min and Qiong.
translations.idiomatic: He next planned his "Three Capitals" rhapsody; when his sister Zuo Fen entered the harem the family relocated to Luoyang, and Zuo called on Editorial Director Zhang Zai to gather material on Shu Min and Qiong.

sentences.zh: 遂構思十年，門庭籓溷，皆著筆紙，遇得一句，即便疏之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he conceived it for ten years; gate, courtyard, fence, and privy all had brush and paper—whenever he obtained a line he at once wrote it down.
translations.idiomatic: He brooded on the work a full decade; brush and paper littered gate, yard, fence, and latrine—every stray couplet was recorded on the spot.

sentences.zh: 自以所見不博，求為秘書郎。

translations.literal: He himself thought what he had seen was not broad; he sought appointment as Palace Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Feeling his reading still too narrow, he secured a post as palace secretary for access to the imperial library.

sentences.zh: 及賦成，時人未之重。

translations.literal: When the fu was finished, people of the time did not yet esteem it.
translations.idiomatic: When the rhapsody was done, contemporaries still shrugged it off.

sentences.zh: 思自以其作不謝班張，恐以人廢言，安定皇甫謐有高譽，思造而示之。

translations.literal: Si himself thought his work did not yield to Ban and Zhang; he feared people would discard the words because of the man—Huangfu Mi of Anding had a lofty reputation, and Si visited and showed it to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo believed his work matched Ban Gu and Zhang Heng yet feared dismissal on account of his homely looks, so he brought the manuscript to the renowned Huangfu Mi of Anding.

sentences.zh: 謐稱善，為其賦序。

translations.literal: Mi praised it as good and composed a preface to his fu.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu praised it and supplied a preface.

sentences.zh: 張載為注《魏都》，劉逵注《吳》《蜀》而序之曰：「觀中古以來為賦者多矣，相如《子虛》擅名于前，班固《兩都》理勝其辭，張衡《二京》文過其意。

translations.literal: Zhang Zai annotated the "Wei Capital"; Liu Kui annotated the "Wu" and "Shu" sections and prefaced them, saying, "Since middle antiquity many have composed fu: Xiangru's 'Sir Vacuous' monopolized fame early; Ban Gu's 'Two Capitals' had principle surpassing its phrasing; Zhang Heng's 'Two Capitals' had pattern exceeding its ideas.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zai glossed the Wei section; Liu Kui annotated Wu and Shu and wrote a preface: "Fu writers crowd the middle ages—Sima Xiangru's 'Sir Vacuous' claimed first glory; Ban Gu's twin capitals privilege argument over diction; Zhang Heng's pair favors ornament over thought.

sentences.zh: 至若此賦，擬議數家，傅辭會義，抑多精緻，非夫研核者不能練其旨，非夫博物者不能統其異。

translations.literal: As for this fu, it models several masters, spreads phrasing and joins meanings—indeed much is refined; unless one examines closely one cannot master its aim; unless one broadly knows things one cannot unite its differences.
translations.idiomatic: This piece, however, distills many models and weaves diction with doctrine at rare finesse—only a painstaking reader grasps its argument, only a scholar of wide learning commands its diversity.

sentences.zh: 世咸貴遠而賤近，莫肯用心於明物。

translations.literal: The age all esteems the distant and despises the near; none is willing to apply mind to clarifying things.
translations.idiomatic: People honor the remote past and scorn the present, unwilling to labor over factual truth.

sentences.zh: 斯文吾有異焉，故聊以餘思為其引詁，亦猶胡廣之於《官箴》，蔡邕之於《典引》也。

translations.literal: On this text I have a different view; therefore briefly with remaining thought I supply its introduction and gloss—it is also like Hu Guang with regard to the 'Official Admonition,' Cai Yong with regard to the 'Canon Introduction.'"
translations.idiomatic: I take a different view of this text, so I lend what wit remains to introduce and gloss it—much as Hu Guang annotated the "Official Admonitions" or Cai Yong the "Canon Preface."

sentences.zh: 」陳留衛權又為思賦作《略解》，序曰：「余觀《三都》之賦，言不苟華，必經典要，品物殊類，稟之圖籍；

translations.literal: " Wei Quan of Chenliu further composed for Si's fu a "Brief Explication," prefacing it: "I have viewed the fu 'Three Capitals': its words do not recklessly flower—they must pass through canonical essentials; the categories of things are diverse classes, received from charts and records;
translations.idiomatic: " Wei Quan of Chenliu also wrote a "Brief Explication" for Zuo's work, opening: "Reading the 'Three Capitals,' one finds no idle flourish—every line rests on canonical authority; each thing catalogued comes straight from the atlases and histories.

sentences.zh: 辭義瑰瑋，良可貴也。

translations.literal: its phrasing and meaning are rare and grand—truly to be prized.
translations.idiomatic: The language is splendid and the sense monumental—work of real worth.

sentences.zh: 有晉征士故太子中庶子安定皇甫謐，西州之逸士，耽籍樂道，高尚其事，覽斯文而慷慨，為之都序。

translations.literal: There is Jin reclusive scholar, former Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent Huangfu Mi of Anding, a retired gentleman of the western provinces who delighted in texts and rejoiced in the Way, holding his pursuits lofty—reading this refined writing he grew impassioned and composed for it a general preface.
translations.idiomatic: The recluse Huangfu Mi of Anding—once junior mentor to the crown prince—western gentleman lost in books and the Way, lofty in purpose, read these lines with beating heart and supplied the overarching preface.

sentences.zh: 中書著作郎安平張載、中書郎濟南劉逵，並以經學洽博，才章美茂，咸皆悅玩，為之訓詁；

translations.literal: Gentleman Compiler Zhang Zai of Anping and Gentleman of the Palace Writers Liu Kui of Jinan—both by classical learning were broadly versed, their talent and pattern rich and lush—all alike delighted in it and played with it, producing glosses for it;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zai of Anping and Liu Kui of Jinan—court compilers steeped in the classics, gifted stylists—each delighted in the text and drafted scholarly commentary;

sentences.zh: 其山川土域，草木鳥獸，奇怪珍異，僉皆研精所由，紛散其義矣。

translations.literal: as to its mountains and rivers, soil and regions, plants and trees, birds and beasts, strange and precious marvels—all alike investigated with refinement whence they came, scattering and unfolding their meanings.
translations.idiomatic: every landscape, soil, plant, beast, and curiosity they traced to source, unpacking sense after sense.

sentences.zh: 余嘉其文，不能默已，聊藉二子之遺忘，又為之《略解》，祗增煩重，覽者闕焉。

translations.literal: I admire its pattern and cannot be silent; briefly borrowing where those two sons left gaps, I again composed for it a "Brief Explication"—only adding annoyance and burden; let readers omit it.
translations.idiomatic: I admire the piece too deeply to stay mute; picking up where Zhang and Liu left off I added this "Brief Explication"—knowing it only piles dutiful clutter on readers who may skip it.

sentences.zh: 」自是之後，盛重于時，文多不載。

translations.literal: " From this time onward it was greatly esteemed in its age—much of the text is not recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: " After that the work commanded enormous esteem (most of the prose is omitted here).

sentences.zh: 司空張華見而歎曰：「班張之流也。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Zhang Hua saw it and sighed, saying, "Of the class of Ban and Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zhang Hua exclaimed, "This belongs with Ban Gu and Zhang Heng.

sentences.zh: 使讀之者盡而有餘，久而更新。

translations.literal: It causes those who read it to exhaust yet still have surplus; long enduring yet anew.
translations.idiomatic: Readers finish yet feel there is more; revisit after years and it still feels fresh.

sentences.zh: 」於是豪貴之家競相傳寫，洛陽為之紙貴。

translations.literal: " Thereupon houses of the mighty and noble vied to copy and circulate it; Luoyang for this reason had costly paper.
translations.idiomatic: " Noble households scrambled to copy it until Luoyang ran short of paper—a story still told today.

sentences.zh: 初，陸機入洛，欲為此賦，聞思作之，撫掌而笑，與弟雲書曰：「此間有傖父，欲作《三都賦》，須其成，當以覆酒甕耳。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Lu Ji entered Luoyang he wished to compose this fu; hearing Si was composing it, he clapped his hands and laughed, writing to his younger brother Yun: "Here there is a boorish fellow who wishes to compose the 'Fu on the Three Capitals'; wait until it is finished—we shall use it to cover wine jars."
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Ji first reached Luoyang he meant to write his own "Three Capitals"; learning Zuo was at work he laughed aloud and wrote Lu Yun: "Some rustic here thinks he can compose that rhapsody—when he's done we'll line the wine jars with it."

sentences.zh: 」及思賦出，機絕歎伏，以為不能加也，遂輟筆焉。

translations.literal: " When Si's fu appeared, Ji utterly sighed and submitted, thinking he could not surpass it—thereupon he stopped his brush.
translations.idiomatic: " Once Zuo's piece appeared, Lu Ji conceded outright that he could not better it and abandoned his own draft.

sentences.zh: 秘書監賈謐請講《漢書》，謐誅，退居宜春裏，專意典籍。

translations.literal: Palace Library Supervisor Jia Mi invited him to lecture on the Han History; when Mi was executed, [Si] retired to live in Yichun Ward and devoted intent attention to classical writings.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Mi, director of the palace library, asked him to lecture on the Han History; after Jia's execution Zuo withdrew to Yichun Ward and buried himself in books.

sentences.zh: 齊王冏命為記室督，辭疾，不就。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi, Sima Jiong, ordered him to be Recorder-in-Chief; he declined citing illness and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Jiong, Prince of Qi, offered him chief recorder; Zuo pleaded illness and refused.

sentences.zh: 及張方縱暴都邑，舉家適冀州。

translations.literal: When Zhang Fang wantonly ravaged the capital region, he moved the whole household to Ji province.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Fang terrorized the capital the entire family fled north into Ji province.

sentences.zh: 數歲，以疾終。

translations.literal: After several years he ended by illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness a few years later.

sentences.zh: 趙至

translations.literal: Zhao Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhi

sentences.zh: 趙至，字景真，代郡人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Zhi, style Jingzhen, was a man of Dai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhi, courtesy name Jingzhen, was a native of Dai commandery.

sentences.zh: 寓居洛陽。

translations.literal: He dwelled sojourning in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: His family had settled in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 緱氏令初到官，至年十三，與母同觀。

translations.literal: When the magistrate of Goushi first arrived at his post, Zhi was thirteen years old and together with his mother watched.
translations.idiomatic: When the new magistrate of Goushi took office, thirteen-year-old Zhao went with his mother to watch the procession.

sentences.zh: 母曰：「汝先世本非微賤，世亂流離，遂為士伍耳。

translations.literal: His mother said, "Your ancestors were originally not lowly; age disorder scattering separation—thereupon they became common soldiers, that's all.
translations.idiomatic: His mother said, "Our forebears were never humble folk; war uprooted the clan until they sank into the ranks—that is all.

sentences.zh: 爾後能如此不？

translations.literal: Can you afterward be like this or not?
translations.idiomatic: Will you rise above this life or not?

sentences.zh: 」至感母言，詣師受業。

translations.literal: " Zhi was moved by his mother's words and went to a teacher to receive instruction.
translations.idiomatic: " Moved deeply, Zhao sought out a tutor.

sentences.zh: 聞父耕叱牛聲，投書而泣。

translations.literal: Hearing his father's plowing shout at the ox, he cast aside his book and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he heard his father shouting at the ox in the field he dropped his primer and wept.

sentences.zh: 師怪問之，至曰：「我小未能榮養，使老父不免勤苦。

translations.literal: The teacher wondered and asked him; Zhi said, "I am young and unable yet to honor and support [them], causing my aged father not to avoid toil and bitterness.
translations.idiomatic: His teacher asked why; Zhao answered, "I am too young to earn honor or keep my parents fed—the old man still toils because of me.

sentences.zh: 」師甚異之。

translations.literal: " The teacher greatly considered him unusual.
translations.idiomatic: " The instructor marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 年十四，詣洛陽，遊太學，遇嵇康于學寫石經，徘徊視之，不能去，而請問姓名。

translations.literal: At age fourteen he went to Luoyang and roamed the Imperial Academy; he encountered Ji Kang at the academy copying the stone classics—hovering he gazed, unable to leave, and requested to ask his name.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he entered the capital and the Imperial Academy, where he found Ji Kang transcribing the stone classics; Zhao circled, unable to tear himself away, and begged the stranger's name.

sentences.zh: 康曰：「年少何以問邪？

translations.literal: Kang said, "Youth—why do you ask?"
translations.idiomatic: Ji Kang said, "What is a boy like you doing asking?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「觀君風器非常，所以問耳。

translations.literal: " [Zhi] said, "Observing your air and bearing is not ordinary—therefore I ask, that's all.
translations.idiomatic: " "Your bearing is like no other—that is why I asked."

sentences.zh: 」康異而告之。

translations.literal: " Kang considered it strange and told him [his name].
translations.idiomatic: " Ji Kang, intrigued, told him who he was.

sentences.zh: 後乃亡到山陽，求康不得而還。

translations.literal: Afterward he fled to Shanyang, sought Kang but did not find him, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He later ran away to Shanyang hoping to find Ji Kang but failed and trudged home.

sentences.zh: 又將遠學，母禁之，至遂陽狂，走三五里，輒追得之。

translations.literal: Again he was about to study far away; his mother forbade him—Zhi thereupon feigned madness, ran five or three li, and each time was pursued and caught.
translations.idiomatic: When he tried to leave for distant study his mother forbade it, so he feigned madness and bolted a few miles—each time she ran him down.

sentences.zh: 年十六，遊鄴，復與康相遇，隨康還山陽，改名浚，字允元。

translations.literal: At age sixteen he roamed Ye; again he encountered Kang and followed Kang back to Shanyang—he changed his name to Jun, style Yuanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he wandered to Ye, met Ji Kang again, followed him home to Shanyang, and adopted the name Zhao Jun, courtesy name Yuanyuan.

sentences.zh: 康每曰：「卿頭小而銳，童子白黑分明，有白起之風矣。

translations.literal: Kang often said, "Your head is small and keen; as a boy black and white were distinct in your eyes—you have the air of Bai Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Kang used to tell him, "That sharp little head of yours, those bright eyes even as a boy—you have something of Bai Qi about you."

sentences.zh: 」及康卒，至詣魏興見太守張嗣宗，甚被優遇。

translations.literal: " When Kang died, Zhi went to Wei Xing and visited Administrator Zhang Sizong and was greatly favored.
translations.idiomatic: After Ji Kang's execution Zhao traveled to Wei Xing and called on Prefect Zhang Sizong, who treated him with exceptional kindness.

sentences.zh: 嗣宗遷江夏相，隨到溳川，欲因入吳，而嗣宗卒，乃向遼西而占戶焉。

translations.literal: Sizong was transferred to be minister of Jiangxia; [Zhi] followed him to Yun River, intending thereby to enter Wu, but Sizong died—thereupon he headed toward Liaoxi and registered his household there.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang rose to governor of Jiangxia, Zhao followed him to the Yun basin hoping to cross into Wu; Zhang died before they could go, so Zhao drifted to Liaoxi and settled his household register there.

sentences.zh: 初，至與康兄子蕃友善，及將遠適，乃與蕃書敘離，並陳其志曰：

translations.literal: Earlier Zhi had been friendly with Kang's elder brother's son Fan; when he was about to go far away he wrote Fan a letter narrating parting and stating his intent, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He had long befriended Ji Kang's nephew Ji Fan; before leaving for good he sent Fan a farewell letter laying bare his purpose:

sentences.zh: 至身長七尺四寸，論議精辯，有從橫才氣。

translations.literal: Zhi's body was seven chi four cun in height; in discourse and debate he was refined and acute and had the talent-air of vertical-horizontal persuaders.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao stood seven feet four inches tall; his speech was sharp and incisive in the manner of a wandering strategist.

sentences.zh: 遼西舉郡計吏，到洛，與父相遇。

translations.literal: Liaoxi nominated him commandery accounting clerk; arriving at Luoyang he encountered his father.
translations.idiomatic: Liaoxi recommended him as chief clerk for fiscal reporting; in Luoyang he unexpectedly met his father.

sentences.zh: 時母已亡，父欲令其宦立，弗之告，仍戒以不歸，至乃還遼西。

translations.literal: At that time his mother had already died; his father wished to cause him to establish himself through office and did not inform him of this, still enjoining him not to return—Zhi thereupon returned to Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: His mother had died without his knowledge—his father hid the news so Zhao could establish a career and forbade him to come home; Zhao therefore turned back toward Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 幽州三辟部從事，斷九獄，見稱精審。

translations.literal: Youzhou thrice summoned him as staff attendant to the ministry; he adjudicated nine cases and was praised as rigorous.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhou repeatedly appointed him section aide; he closed nine criminal cases and earned praise for meticulous judgment.

sentences.zh: 太康中，以良吏赴洛，方知母亡。

translations.literal: In the Taikang era, because he was a good official he went to Luoyang—only then did he learn his mother had died.
translations.idiomatic: During Taikang he qualified as an exemplary official and was summoned to court—only then did he learn his mother was gone.

sentences.zh: 初，至自恥士伍，欲以宦學立名，期於榮養。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhi himself was ashamed of being a common soldier and wished by office and learning to establish a name, aiming at honored support.
translations.idiomatic: Once ashamed of his commoner's station, he had hoped office and scholarship would win honor enough to support his parents in style.

sentences.zh: 既而其志不就，號憤慟哭，歐血而卒，時年三十七。

translations.literal: But thereafter his aim was not realized; he wailed in rage and wept in grief, vomited blood and died—at that time age thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: When that dream collapsed he howled and wept until blood burst from his throat; he died at thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 鄒湛

translations.literal: Zou Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Zhan

sentences.zh: 鄒湛，字潤甫，南陽新野人也。

translations.literal: Zou Zhan, style Runfu, was a man of Xinye in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Zhan, courtesy name Runfu, hailed from Xinye in Nanyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 父軌，魏左將軍。

translations.literal: His father Gui was Left General of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zou Gui had served Wei as Left General.

sentences.zh: 湛少以才學知名，仕魏曆通事郎、太學博士。

translations.literal: In youth Zhan was famed for talent and learning; serving Wei he passed through Communicator Gentleman and Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Celebrated young for breadth of learning, he served Wei as communicator gentleman and erudite at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，轉尚書郎、廷尉平、征南從事中郎，深為羊祜所器重。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi he transferred to Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, Administrator of Justice Evaluation, and Staff Officer on the South Expedition—he was deeply prized by Yang Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taishi he moved through masters-of-writing posts, justice reviewer, and aide on the southern campaign—Yang Hu esteemed him greatly.

sentences.zh: 入為太子中庶子。

translations.literal: He entered [court] as Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was then called in as junior mentor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 太康中，拜散騎常侍，出補渤海太守，轉太傅楊駿長史，遷侍中。

translations.literal: In the Taikang era he was appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, went out to fill the post of governor of Bohai, transferred to be chief clerk to Grand Tutor Yang Jun, and was promoted to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taikang he became cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, then governor of Bohai, later chief secretary to Grand Tutor Yang Jun, and finally palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 駿誅，以僚佐免官。

translations.literal: When Jun was executed, by being a subordinate staff member he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun's fall cost him his post as a member of the discredited staff.

sentences.zh: 尋起為散騎常侍、國子祭酒，轉少府。

translations.literal: Soon he was raised to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Libationer of the National University, and transferred to Minister of the Lesser Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reinstated as cavalier attendant and libationer of the Imperial College, then moved to head the Lesser Treasury.

sentences.zh: 元康末卒，所著詩及論事議二十五首，為時所重。

translations.literal: He died at the end of Yuankang; his writings—poetry and discussion pieces on affairs in twenty-five pieces—were valued by the age.
translations.idiomatic: He died near the close of Yuankang; twenty-five poems and policy essays won wide respect.

sentences.zh: 初，湛嘗夢見一人，自稱甄舒仲，餘無所言，如此非一。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhan once dreamed of a man who called himself Zhen Shuzhong—otherwise nothing was said; it was so not once.
translations.idiomatic: Zou repeatedly dreamed of a figure calling himself Zhen Shuzhong who said nothing more—the dream returned again and again.

sentences.zh: 久之，乃悟曰：「吾宅西有積土敗瓦，其中必有死人。

translations.literal: After a long time he at last understood, saying, "West of my residence there is piled earth and ruined tile—inside there must be a dead person.
translations.idiomatic: At length he understood: "West of my house lie rubble piles—someone lies buried beneath them."

sentences.zh: 甄舒仲者，予舍西土瓦中人也。

translations.literal: As for Zhen Shuzhong—he is a person among the earth and tile west of my house.
translations.idiomatic: "Zhen Shuzhong" is the restless soul beneath the rubble west of my gate.

sentences.zh: 」檢之，果然，厚加斂葬。

translations.literal: " Investigating it, it was indeed so; he generously ordered burial rites.
translations.idiomatic: They dug and found him, then laid the bones to rest with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 葬畢，遂夢此人來謝。

translations.literal: When burial was finished, thereupon he dreamed this person came to thank him.
translations.idiomatic: That night the figure visited his dreams to give thanks.

sentences.zh: 子捷，字太應，亦有文才。

translations.literal: His son Jie, style Taiying, also had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zou Jie, courtesy name Taiying, inherited literary gifts.

sentences.zh: 永康中，為散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: In the Yongkang era he was Gentleman of Cavalier Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongkang he served as gentleman of cavalier attendance.

sentences.zh: 及趙王倫篡逆，捷與陸機等俱作禪文。

translations.literal: When Prince Zhao Sima Lun usurped in rebellion, Jie together with Lu Ji and others jointly composed the abdication document.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Zhao Lun seized the throne, Zou Jie joined Lu Ji and others in drafting the forced abdication edict.

sentences.zh: 倫誅，坐下廷尉，遇赦免。

translations.literal: When Lun was executed, [Jie] sat as defendant before the Commandant of Justice; encountering amnesty he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Lun's execution landed him before the commandant of justice; an amnesty spared him.

sentences.zh: 後為太傅參軍。

translations.literal: Later he became Army Adjutant to the Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as adjutant on the grand tutor's staff.

sentences.zh: 永嘉末，卒。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongjia he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the final years of Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 棗據

translations.literal: Zao Ju.
translations.idiomatic: Zao Ju

sentences.zh: 棗據，字道彥，潁川長社人也。

translations.literal: Zao Ju, style Daoyan, was a man of Changshe in Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zao Ju, courtesy name Daoyan, came from Changshe in Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 本姓棘，其先避仇改焉。

translations.literal: Originally the surname was Ji; his ancestors changed it to flee blood-feud.
translations.idiomatic: The clan originally bore the surname Ji but changed it generations ago to escape a vendetta.

sentences.zh: 父叔禕，魏钜鹿太守。

translations.literal: His father Shu Yi was governor of Julu in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zao Shuwei governed Julu under Wei.

sentences.zh: 據美容貌，善文辭。

translations.literal: Ju had handsome facial appearance and was skilled in literary phrasing.
translations.idiomatic: Handsome and eloquent, he cut a striking figure at court.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，辟大將軍府，出為山陽令，有政績。

translations.literal: At the capping age he was summoned to the Grand General's headquarters; he went out as magistrate of Shanyang and had administrative achievements.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he entered the grand general's bureau, then governed Shanyang county with a solid record.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書郎，轉右丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Gentleman of the Masters of Writing and transferred to Assistant Director on the Right.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to gentleman of the masters of writing and then assistant director on the right.

sentences.zh: 賈充伐吳，請為從事中郎。

translations.literal: When Jia Chong campaigned against Wu he requested [Ju] as Staff Officer.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Chong drafted him as middle staff officer for the Wu campaign.

sentences.zh: 軍還，徙黃門侍郎、冀州刺史、太子中庶子。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was shifted to Gentleman of the Yellow Gates, Inspector of Ji province, and Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After the troops came home he served successively as gentleman at the Yellow Gates, Ji provincial inspector, and junior mentor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 太康中卒，時年五十餘。

translations.literal: He died in the Taikang era at age over fifty.
translations.idiomatic: He died during Taikang in his early fifties.

sentences.zh: 所著詩賦論四十五首，遇亂多亡失。

translations.literal: What he composed—poetry, fu, and discourses in forty-five pieces—when encountering turmoil mostly perished and was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Forty-five poems, rhapsodies, and essays bore his name; most vanished in the wars.

sentences.zh: 子腆，字玄方，亦以文章顯。

translations.literal: His son Tian, style Xuanfang, also by literature showed distinction.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zao Tian, courtesy name Xuanfang, likewise won fame as a writer.

sentences.zh: 永嘉中為襄城太守。

translations.literal: In the Yongjia era he was governor of Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongjia he governed Xiangcheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 弟嵩，字台產，才藝尤美，為太子中庶子、散騎常侍，為石勒所殺。

translations.literal: Younger brother Song, style Taichan—talent and arts especially fine—was Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent and Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary; he was killed by Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Zao Song, courtesy name Taichan, combined literary and artistic gifts; he served as junior mentor and cavalier attendant-in-ordinary until Shi Le had him executed.

sentences.zh: 褚陶

translations.literal: Chu Tao.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Tao

sentences.zh: 褚陶，字季雅，吳郡錢塘人也。

translations.literal: Chu Tao, style Jiya, was a man of Qiantang in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Tao, courtesy name Jiya, came from Qiantang in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 弱不好弄，少而聰慧，清淡閑默，以墳典自娛。

translations.literal: In youth he did not like playing; young he was clever and wise, pure and quiet, leisurely silent, taking the tomb classics as self-amusement.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy he shunned rough games; precocious and reflective, he preferred quiet study of the classical corpus.

sentences.zh: 年十三，作《鷗鳥》、《水磑》二賦，見者奇之。

translations.literal: At age thirteen he composed two fu, "Gulls" and "Water Mill"; those who saw them deemed them marvelous.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he wrote the rhapsodies "Gulls" and "The Water Mill," astonishing everyone who read them.

sentences.zh: 陶嘗謂所親曰：「聖賢備在黃卷中，舍此何求！

translations.literal: Tao once said to those close to him, "Sages and worthies are fully contained in yellow-bound scrolls—apart from this what do we seek!
translations.idiomatic: He told friends, "Everything worth knowing sits between yellow covers—what else is there to chase?

sentences.zh: 」州郡辟，不就。

translations.literal: " The province and commandery summoned him; he did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: " Provincial posts came calling; he declined them all.

sentences.zh: 吳平，召補尚書郎。

translations.literal: When Wu was pacified he was summoned to fill Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu surrendered he was appointed gentleman of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 張華見之，謂陸機曰：「君兄弟龍躍雲津，顧彥先鳳鳴朝陽，謂東南之寶已盡，不意復見褚生。

translations.literal: When Zhang Hua saw him he said to Lu Ji, "Your lordship's brothers leap as dragons at the cloud ford; Gu Yanxian cries as the phoenix at morning sun—I thought the treasures of the southeast were exhausted; I did not expect again to see Master Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua told Lu Ji, "Your clan springs like dragons across the cloudy ford; Gu Yanxian sings like the phoenix at dawn—I assumed the southeast had spent every jewel of talent, then Chu Tao appeared."

sentences.zh: 」機曰：「公但未睹不鳴不躍者耳。

translations.literal: " Ji said, "My lord only has not yet seen those who neither cry nor leap.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji replied, "You simply have not met everyone who keeps silent and still."

sentences.zh: 」華曰：「故知延州之德不孤，川嶽之寶不匱矣。

translations.literal: " Hua said, "Thus I know the virtue of Yanzhou is not solitary; treasures of rivers and mountains are not exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua answered, "So virtue like Ji Zha's need not stand alone; every river and peak still hides treasure."

sentences.zh: 」遷九真太守，轉中尉。

translations.literal: " He was promoted governor of Jiuzhen and transferred to Commandant of the Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Chu later governed Jiuzhen before becoming metropolitan commandant.

sentences.zh: 年五十五卒。

translations.literal: At age fifty-five he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 王沉

translations.literal: Wang Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chen

sentences.zh: 王沉，字彥伯，高平人也。

translations.literal: Wang Chen, style Yanbo, was a man of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chen, courtesy name Yanbo, came from Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 少有俊才，出於寒素，不能隨俗沈浮，為時豪所抑。

translations.literal: In youth he had outstanding talent; he came from humble plain background and could not float or sink with custom—he was suppressed by the powerful of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Gifted but from an obscure house, he refused to curry favor with great families and paid for it in obscurity.

sentences.zh: 仕郡文學掾，鬱鬱不得志，乃作《釋時論》，其辭曰：

translations.literal: He served as commandery Instructor Clerk, depressed without realizing his aims—thereupon he composed "Discourse Explaining the Age," its words saying:
translations.idiomatic: He held only the minor post of instructor to his commandery and, bitterly frustrated, wrote "On Explaining Our Times," which opens:

sentences.zh: 是時王政陵遲，官才失實，君子多退而窮處，遂終於里閭。

translations.literal: At this time royal administration declined; official talent lost substance; gentlemen mostly withdrew and dwelt in hardship—thereupon they ended in hamlets.
translations.idiomatic: Royal government had slackened; offices went to mediocrities; men of worth withdrew to rustic lanes and died unheard.

sentences.zh: 元康初，松滋令吳郡蔡洪字叔開，有才名，作《孤奮論》，與《釋時》意同，讀之者莫不歎息焉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuankang, Cai Hong of Wu commandery, style Shukai, magistrate of Songzi—had a reputation for talent—composed "Discourse of Lone Exertion"; with "Explaining the Age" the intent was the same—those who read it none did not sigh.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuankang Cai Hong of Wu—magistrate of Songzi, courtesy name Shukai—won fame for "Discourse on Relentless Effort," echoing Wang's themes and drawing sighs from every reader.

sentences.zh: 張翰

translations.literal: Zhang Han.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Han

sentences.zh: 張翰，字季鷹，吳郡吳人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Han, style Jiying, was a man of Wu in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Han, courtesy name Jiying, came from Wu county in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 父儼，吳大鴻臚。

translations.literal: His father Yan was Grand Herald of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhang Yan had served Wu as grand herald.

sentences.zh: 翰有清才，善屬文，而縱任不拘，時人號為「江東步兵。

translations.literal: Han had pure talent, skilled in composing texts, yet unrestrained and unbound—people of the time titled him "Infantry Lieutenant east of the Yangzi."
translations.idiomatic: His prose was lucid and his habits bohemian; contemporaries nicknamed him "Wu Kingdom's Infantry Captain"

sentences.zh: 」會稽賀循赴命入洛，經吳閶門，於船中彈琴。

translations.literal: " He Xun of Kuaiji answered summons and entered Luoyang; passing Wu's Chang Gate he played the zither in the boat.
translations.idiomatic: —alluding to Ruan Ji. One day He Xun of Kuaiji traveled to Luoyang under summons; mooring at Wu's Chang Gate he played his lute on board.

sentences.zh: 翰初不相識，乃就循言譚，便大相欽悅。

translations.literal: Han at first did not know him; thereupon he approached Xun and conversed—at once they greatly admired each other.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang did not know him at first but stepped aboard to talk and found an instant soulmate.

sentences.zh: 問循，知其入洛，翰曰：「吾亦有事北京。

translations.literal: He asked Xun; learning that he was entering Luoyang, Han said, "I too have business in the northern capital.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that He was bound for the capital, Zhang said, "I have errands in the north as well."

sentences.zh: 」便同載即去，而不告家人。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they rode in the same carriage and left immediately, without telling family members.
translations.idiomatic: " They shared a carriage and vanished without a word to kin.

sentences.zh: 齊王冏辟為大司馬東曹掾。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi, Sima Jiong, summoned him as Clerk of the East Bureau under the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Jiong, Prince of Qi, appointed him clerk in the grand marshal's eastern bureau.

sentences.zh: 冏時執權，翰謂同郡顧榮曰：「天下紛紛，禍難未已。

translations.literal: When Jiong held power Han said to Gu Rong of the same commandery, "All under heaven is tumultuous; disasters are not yet ended.
translations.idiomatic: While Sima Jiong dominated court, Zhang warned fellow Wu native Gu Rong, "The realm boils and the killing is not over.

sentences.zh: 夫有四海之名者，求退良難。

translations.literal: For one who has fame within the four seas, seeking withdrawal is truly difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Renown across the empire makes retreat almost impossible.

sentences.zh: 吾本山林間人，無望于時。

translations.literal: I am originally a man among mountains and forests—I have no expectation in this age.
translations.idiomatic: I belong among hills and streams, not this court.

sentences.zh: 子善以明防前，以智慮後。

translations.literal: You, sir, are good at guarding what lies ahead with clarity and pondering what follows with wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: You read trouble coming and plan what follows—skills I lack.

sentences.zh: 」榮執其手，愴然曰：「吾亦與子采南山蕨，飲三江水耳。

translations.literal: " Rong grasped his hand and mournfully said, "I too with you would gather bracken on South Mountain and drink the Three Rivers' water, that's all.
translations.idiomatic: " Gu seized his hand and said sadly, "I would gladly pick ferns on South Mountain with you and drink only river water."

sentences.zh: 」翰因見秋風起，乃思吳中菰菜、蓴羹、鱸魚膾，曰：「人生貴得適志，何能羈宦數千里以要名爵乎！

translations.literal: " Han because he saw the autumn wind arise then thought of wild rice shoots, water-shield soup, and perch sashimi in Wu—he said, "In human life what is prized is obtaining one's mind's ease—how can one be tied to office thousands of li to seek rank and title!
translations.idiomatic: " When autumn wind rose he craved Wu water-shield soup, wild rice, and sliced perch. "Life is too short to chain yourself a thousand miles from home for a hollow title!"

sentences.zh: 」遂命駕而歸。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he ordered carriage and returned.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered his carriage and rode east that same day.

sentences.zh: 著《首丘賦》，文多不載。

translations.literal: He composed the "Fu on Longing for the Burrow Mound"; much of the text is not recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote "Rhapsody on the Hill of Home" (largely omitted here).

sentences.zh: 俄而冏敗，人皆謂之見機。

translations.literal: Soon Jiong was defeated; people all called him one who saw the moment.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Jiong fell soon afterward everyone called Zhang prescient.

sentences.zh: 然府以其輒去，除吏名。

translations.literal: Yet the bureau because he abruptly left struck his name from the clerks.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry nevertheless struck him from the rolls for desertion.

sentences.zh: 翰任心自適，不求當世。

translations.literal: Han followed his heart and suited himself, not seeking validation from his age.
translations.idiomatic: He followed his mood and cared nothing for reputation among his peers.

sentences.zh: 或謂之曰：「卿乃可縱適一時，獨不為身後名邪？

translations.literal: Someone said to him, "You indeed may indulge ease for a moment—do you alone not act for posthumous fame?
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked, "You indulge the moment—have you no thought for how posterity will judge you?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「使我有身後名，不如即時一杯酒。

translations.literal: " He replied, "Let me have posthumous fame—better an immediate cup of wine.
translations.idiomatic: " "I'd trade any posthumous fame for another cup of wine tonight."

sentences.zh: 」時人貴其曠達。

translations.literal: " People of the time prized his broad openness.
translations.idiomatic: " His candor passed for profundity in that cynical age.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，遭母憂，哀毀過禮。

translations.literal: By nature he was supremely filial; encountering mourning for his mother he sorrowed and wasted beyond ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply filial, he mourned his mother past what ritual allowed.

sentences.zh: 年五十七卒。

translations.literal: At age fifty-seven he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 其文筆數十篇行於世。

translations.literal: His literary brushings several tens of pieces circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen essays and poems survived him.

sentences.zh: 庾闡

translations.literal: Yu Chan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chan

sentences.zh: 庾闡，字仲初，潁川鄢陵人也。

translations.literal: Yu Chan, style Zhongchu, was a man of Yanling in Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chan, courtesy name Zhongchu, hailed from Yanling in Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 祖輝，安北長史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hui was chief clerk to the General Who Guards the North.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yu Hui had served as chief clerk on the staff of the general who guards the north.

sentences.zh: 父東，以勇力聞。

translations.literal: His father Dong was famed for courage and strength.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yu Dong was famed for raw strength.

sentences.zh: 武帝時，有西域健胡趫捷無敵，晉人莫敢與校。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wu's time there was a stalwart Hu from the Western Regions, agile and unmatched—people of Jin none dared contend with him.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu a Western Regions wrestler appeared whom no Jin challenger could best.

sentences.zh: 帝募勇士，惟東應選，遂撲殺之，名震殊俗。

translations.literal: The emperor recruited brave warriors—only Dong answered selection—thereupon he threw and killed him; his name shook foreign customs.
translations.idiomatic: The throne sought brawlers; Yu Dong alone volunteered and threw the man dead—his fame echoed beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 闡好學，九歲能屬文。

translations.literal: Chan loved learning; at age nine he could compose texts.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chan loved books and composed polished essays at nine.

sentences.zh: 少隨舅孫氏過江。

translations.literal: In youth he followed his maternal uncle's Sun clan in crossing the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he crossed the Yangzi with his mother's Sun kin.

sentences.zh: 母隨兄肇為樂安長史，在項城。

translations.literal: His mother followed elder brother Zhao who was chief clerk to Le'an—at Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: His mother lived with her brother in Xiangcheng while he served as chief clerk in Le'an.

sentences.zh: 永嘉末，為石勒所陷，闡母亦沒。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongjia [the city] was seized by Shi Le—Chan's mother also perished.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Le stormed the city at the close of Yongjia, Yu's mother died in the sack.

sentences.zh: 闡不櫛沐，不婚宦，絕酒肉，垂二十年，鄉親稱之。

translations.literal: Chan did not comb or wash, did not marry or take office, cut off wine and meat—for nearly twenty years village kin praised him.
translations.idiomatic: For nearly twenty years he neither groomed nor married, touched neither meat nor wine—neighbors admired his devotion.

sentences.zh: 州舉秀才，元帝為晉王，辟之，皆不行。

translations.literal: The province nominated him cultivated talent; when Yuan-di was Prince of Jin he summoned him—both times he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: The province ranked him as elite scholar and Prince Yuan-di twice offered posts—Yu refused each summons.

sentences.zh: 後為太宰、西陽王羕掾，累遷尚書郎。

translations.literal: Later he was aide to the Grand Marshal and Prince of Xiyang, Sima Yi—by stages he was promoted to Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined the staff of Sima Yi, Prince of Xiyang and grand marshal, and rose to gentleman of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 蘇峻之難，闡出奔郗鑒，為司空參軍。

translations.literal: During Su Jun's rebellion Chan fled out to Xi Jian and became Army Adjutant to the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Jun seized the capital Yu fled to Xi Jian and served as adjutant on the minister of works' staff.

sentences.zh: 峻平，以功賜爵吉陽縣男，拜彭城內史。

translations.literal: When Jun was pacified, by merit he was granted noble rank as Baron of Jiyang county and appointed Internal Administrator of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: After Su Jun fell Yu earned a barony at Jiyang and appointment as governor of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 鑒復請為從事中郎。

translations.literal: Jian again requested him as Staff Officer.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jian again named him middle staff officer.

sentences.zh: 尋召為散騎侍郎，領大著作。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as Gentleman of Cavalier Attendance and concurrently supervised grand compilation.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became cavalier gentleman-attendant and headed the imperial editorial office.

sentences.zh: 頃之，出補零陵太守，入湘川，吊賈誼。

translations.literal: Shortly he went out to fill governor of Lingling; entering the Xiang river region he mourned Jia Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He then posted out as prefect of Lingling and traveled the Xiang lands to mourn Jia Yi.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：

translations.literal: Its words said:
translations.idiomatic: The piece begins:

sentences.zh: 後以疾，徵拜給事中，復領著作。

translations.literal: Later because of illness he was summoned and appointed Palace Attendant Within the Yellow Gates—again heading compilation.
translations.idiomatic: Ill health later brought him back to court as palace attendant while he again directed the history office.

sentences.zh: 吳國內史虞潭為太伯立碑，闡制其文。

translations.literal: Wu Internal Administrator Yu Tan erected a stele for Taibo—Chan composed its text.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Tan, interior governor of Wu, raised a monument to Taibo, Yu Chan drafted the inscription.

sentences.zh: 又作《揚都賦》，為世所重。

translations.literal: He also composed the "Fu on the Yang Capital"—it was valued by the age.
translations.idiomatic: His "Rhapsody on the Yang Capital" enjoyed enormous esteem.

sentences.zh: 年五十四卒，諡曰貞，所著詩賦銘頌十卷行於世。

translations.literal: At age fifty-four he died; posthumous title was Zhen (Steadfast); what he composed—poetry, fu, inscriptions, and eulogies in ten fascicles—circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-four with the posthumous epithet "Steadfast"; ten fascicles of verse, rhapsodies, and commemorative prose survive.

sentences.zh: 子肅之，亦有文藻著稱，歷給事中、相府記室、湘東太守。

translations.literal: His son Suzhi also had literary ornament and was famed—he passed through Palace Attendant, Recorder of the Minister's headquarters, and governor of Xiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yu Suzhi inherited literary fame, serving as palace attendant, chief recorder on the minister's staff, and governor of Xiangdong.

sentences.zh: 太元中卒。

translations.literal: He died in the Taiyuan era.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Taiyuan reign.

sentences.zh: 曹毗

translations.literal: Cao Pi.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi

sentences.zh: 曹毗，字輔佐，譙國人也。

translations.literal: Cao Pi, style Fuzuo, was a man of Qiao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi, courtesy name Fuzuo, came from Qiao commandery.

sentences.zh: 高祖休，魏大司馬。

translations.literal: His high ancestor Xiu was Grand Marshal of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Cao Xiu had been Wei grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 父識，右軍將軍。

translations.literal: His father Shi was General of the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cao Shi commanded the right army.

sentences.zh: 毗少好文籍，善屬詞賦。

translations.literal: In youth Pi loved literary records and was skilled at composing ci and fu.
translations.idiomatic: Youthful bookworm and polished rhapsodist, he excelled at verse.

sentences.zh: 郡察孝廉，除郎中，蔡謨舉為佐著作郎。

translations.literal: The commandery investigated him as filial and incorrupt; he was appointed Court Gentleman; Cai Mo nominated him as Assistant Gentleman Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: His commandery nominated him as filial and honest; after appointment as court gentleman Cai Mo sponsored him as assistant compiler.

sentences.zh: 父憂去職。

translations.literal: Father mourning caused him to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 服闋，遷句章令，徵拜太學博士。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was promoted magistrate of Gouzhang and summoned as Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period he governed Gouzhang county and was summoned as erudite of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 時桂陽張碩為神女杜蘭香所降，毗因以二篇詩嘲之，並續蘭香歌詩十篇，甚有文彩。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Shuo of Guiyang was visited by the goddess Du Lanxiang—thereupon Pi by means of two poems ridiculed him, and also continued Lanxiang song-poems in ten pieces—very rich in literary color.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Shuo of Guiyang claimed trysts with the goddess Du Lanxiang, Cao answered with two satirical poems and ten sequels to her songs—all dazzlingly wrought.

sentences.zh: 又著《揚都賦》，亞於庾闡。

translations.literal: He also composed the "Fu on the Yang Capital," second only to Yu Chan.
translations.idiomatic: His "Rhapsody on the Yang Capital" ranked just below Yu Chan's celebrated version.

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書郎、鎮軍大將軍從事中郎、下邳太守。

translations.literal: By stages he was promoted Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, Staff Officer on the Army-General Who Garrisoned the Army, and governor of Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through gentleman of the masters of writing, staff officer to the garrisoning general, and governor of Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 以名位不至，著《對儒》以自釋。

translations.literal: Because fame and rank did not arrive, he composed "Response to the Ru" to explain himself.
translations.idiomatic: Frustrated at stalled promotion he wrote "Reply to the Scholars" to justify his choices.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：

translations.literal: Its words said:
translations.idiomatic: It opens:

sentences.zh: 累遷至光祿勳，卒。

translations.literal: By stages he reached Guangluxun—he died.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to minister of the imperial household and died in office.

sentences.zh: 凡所著文筆十五卷，傳於世。

translations.literal: In all what he composed—literary brushings in fifteen fascicles—was transmitted in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen fascicles of prose and verse circulated after him.

sentences.zh: 李充

translations.literal: Li Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong

sentences.zh: 李充，字弘度，江夏人。

translations.literal: Li Chong, style Hongdu, was a man of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong, courtesy name Hongdu, was a native of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 父矩，江州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Ju was Inspector of Jiang province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Li Ju governed Jiang province as inspector.

sentences.zh: 充少孤，其父墓中柏樹嘗為盜賊所斫，充手刃之，由是知名。

translations.literal: Chong in youth was orphaned; the cypress trees at his father's tomb were once damaged by robbers—Chong personally killed the robbers with his own hand—by this he became known.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he tracked down the bandits who had vandalized his father's tomb and slew them with his own blade—news that spread his reputation.

sentences.zh: 善楷書，妙參鐘索，世咸重之。

translations.literal: He was skilled at regular script, subtly referring to Zhong and Suo—the age all prized him.
translations.idiomatic: His regular script rivaled Zhong Yao and Suo Jing—calligraphers everywhere prized his hand.

sentences.zh: 辟丞相王導掾，轉記室參軍。

translations.literal: He was summoned as aide to Chancellor Wang Dao and transferred to Recorder Army Adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao brought him onto the chancellor's staff; he then became recorder-adjutant.

sentences.zh: 幼好刑名之學，深抑虛浮之士，嘗著《學箴》，稱：

translations.literal: In youth he loved the learning of punishment and names; he deeply suppressed empty floating gentlemen—once he composed "Admonition on Learning," saying:
translations.idiomatic: From youth he studied legalist doctrine and scorned fashionable emptiness; his "Admonition on Learning" declares:

sentences.zh: 征北將軍褚裒又引為參軍，充以家貧，苦求外出，裒將許之為縣，試問之，充曰：「窮猿投林，豈暇擇木！

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the North Chu Pou again pulled him in as Army Adjutant; Chong because family was poor bitterly sought to go out—Pou was about to consent to him as county magistrate and tried asking him; Chong said, "A destitute ape casts into forest—how leisure to choose the tree!
translations.idiomatic: Chu Pou of the northern expedition force tried to keep him as adjutant; desperate household finances drove Li to beg a provincial post. When Chu offered a county and asked which he preferred, Li replied, "A hunted ape dives into the forest—there is no leisure to pick the tree!"

sentences.zh: 」乃除縣令，遭母憂。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he was appointed county magistrate—he encountered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: " Chu named him county magistrate; his mother died soon after.

sentences.zh: 服闋，為大著作郎。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he became Chief Gentleman Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he directed the imperial library as chief compiler.

sentences.zh: 于時典籍混亂，充刪除煩重，以類相從，分作四部，甚有條貫，秘閣以為永制。

translations.literal: At that time canonical writings were chaotic; Chong deleted annoyance and redundancy, following category to category, dividing into four departments—very orderly—the secret pavilion took it as perpetual regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Court archives were chaos until Li pruned duplicates, grouped texts by subject, and established the four divisions still used in the palace library.

sentences.zh: 累遷中書侍郎，卒官。

translations.literal: By stages he was promoted Palace Secretariat Gentleman—he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to gentleman of the palace secretariat and died in harness.

sentences.zh: 充注《尚書》及《周易旨》六篇、《釋莊論》上下二篇、詩賦表頌等雜文二百四十首，行於世。

translations.literal: Chong annotated the Documents and six chapters of "Pointers on the Zhou Changes," upper and lower two chapters of "Explaining Zhuangzi," and miscellaneous writings such as poetry, fu, memorials, and eulogies in two hundred forty pieces—circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His corpus includes commentary on the Documents, six essays on the Changes, two treatises on Zhuangzi, and two hundred forty poems, rhapsodies, and state papers.

sentences.zh: 子顒，亦有文義，多所述作，郡舉孝廉。

translations.literal: His son Yong also had literary meaning—many writings—the commandery nominated him filial and incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: His son Li Yong inherited literary gifts and won nomination as filial and honest.

sentences.zh: 充從兄式，以平隱著稱，善楷隸。

translations.literal: Chong's elder cousin Shi was famed for calm reclusion and was skilled at regular and clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Li Shi was noted for quiet integrity and mastery of clerical calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 中興初，仕至侍中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Restoration he served to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Eastern Jin revival he rose to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 袁宏

translations.literal: Yuan Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hong

sentences.zh: 袁宏，字彥伯，侍中猷之孫也。

translations.literal: Yuan Hong, style Yanbo, was grandson of Palace Attendant You.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hong, courtesy name Yanbo, was grandson of the palace attendant Yuan You.

sentences.zh: 父勖，臨汝令。

translations.literal: His father Xu was magistrate of Linru.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuan Xu governed Linru county.

sentences.zh: 宏有逸才，文章絕美，曾為詠史詩，是其風情所寄。

translations.literal: Hong had roaming talent; his writings were supremely beautiful—once he composed poems chanting history—these were where his mood and feeling lodged.
translations.idiomatic: Brilliant and restless, his prose gleamed; his poems on historical themes caught his deepest moods.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧，以運租自業。

translations.literal: In youth orphaned and poor, he took transporting rent grain as his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and destitute, he earned his rice ferrying tax grain.

sentences.zh: 謝尚時鎮牛渚，秋夜乘月，率爾與左右微服泛江。

translations.literal: When Xie Shang was garrisoning Niuzhu, on an autumn night riding the moon he casually with attendants in plain clothes floated on the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: While Xie Shang commanded Niuzhu he slipped onto the river one moonlit autumn night with a handful of companions in disguise.

sentences.zh: 會宏在舫中諷詠，聲既清會，辭又藻拔，遂駐聽久之，遣問焉。

translations.literal: It happened Hong was in a boat chanting aloud—the voice was both clear and harmonious, phrasing also patterned and outstanding—thereupon [Shang] halted and listened long and sent to inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hong's boat drifted past; his voice rang clear and his lines gleamed—Xie ordered the boat stopped and sent men to learn who sang.

sentences.zh: 答云：「是袁臨汝郎誦詩。

translations.literal: Reply said: "It is the Young Gentleman of Linru Yuan reciting poetry.
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "The magistrate of Linru's son is chanting verse."

sentences.zh: 」即其詠史之作也。

translations.literal: " That is his composition chanting history.
translations.idiomatic: " Those were his poems on history.

sentences.zh: 尚傾率有勝致，即迎升舟，與之譚論，申旦不寐，自此名譽日茂。

translations.literal: Shang was unconstrained and had surpassing atmosphere—thereupon he welcomed him to ascend the boat and with him conversed and debated—until dawn without sleeping—from this fame and reputation daily flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted by Yuan's spontaneity, Xie invited him aboard and talked until dawn—overnight Yuan's reputation bloomed.

sentences.zh: 尚為安西將軍、豫州刺史，引宏參其軍事。

translations.literal: When Shang was General Who Guards the West and Inspector of Yu province he drew Hong to join his military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie became general who pacifies the west and inspector of Yu he named Yuan military adviser.

sentences.zh: 累遷大司馬桓溫府記室。

translations.literal: By stages he was promoted Recorder of Grand Marshal Huan Wen's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to chief recorder on Grand Marshal Huan Wen's staff.

sentences.zh: 溫重其文筆，專綜書記。

translations.literal: Wen prized his literary brushings and exclusively supervised correspondence.
translations.idiomatic: Huan prized his pen and gave him sole charge of correspondence.

sentences.zh: 後為《東征賦》，賦末列稱過江諸名德，而獨不載桓彝。

translations.literal: Later he composed the "Eastern Expedition Fu"; at the fu's end he listed and praised the various famed worthies who crossed the Yangzi—but alone did not record Huan Yi.
translations.idiomatic: His "Rhapsody on the Eastern Expedition" praised every eminent migrant minister—but omitted Huan Yi.

sentences.zh: 時伏滔先在溫府，又與宏善，苦諫之。

translations.literal: At that time Fu Tao was earlier in Wen's headquarters and was also good friends with Hong—he bitterly remonstrated him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Tao, already on Huan's staff and friendly with Yuan, pleaded with him to add Huan Yi.

sentences.zh: 宏笑而不答。

translations.literal: Hong smiled and did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan smiled and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 溫知之甚忿，而憚宏一時文宗，不欲令人顯問。

translations.literal: When Wen learned it he was very resentful, yet feared Hong as the age's literary patriarch—he did not wish to cause someone openly to question.
translations.idiomatic: Huan seethed yet hesitated to confront the era's literary arbiter openly.

sentences.zh: 後游青山飲歸，命宏同載，眾為之懼。

translations.literal: Later roaming Green Mountain drinking returning, he ordered Hong to ride in the same carriage—the crowd for this feared.
translations.idiomatic: Later, riding home drunk from Green Mountain, Huan insisted Yuan share his carriage—onlookers trembled for him.

sentences.zh: 行數里，問宏云：「聞君作《東征賦》，多稱先賢，何故不及家君？

translations.literal: Traveling several li he asked Hong saying: "I hear you composed the 'Eastern Expedition Fu,' much praising former worthies—why did you not reach my father?
translations.idiomatic: After a few miles Huan asked, "Your rhapsody praises every worthy—why omit my father?"

sentences.zh: 」宏答曰：「尊公稱謂非下官敢專，既未遑啟，不敢顯之耳。

translations.literal: " Hong replied saying: "Your honored father's title and reference—this lower official does not dare monopolize; since I had not yet leisure to consult, I did not dare display him.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuan answered, "Addressing so exalted a patronage is not mine to decide lightly—without your instruction I dared not presume."

sentences.zh: 」溫疑不實，乃曰：「君欲為何辭？

translations.literal: " Wen doubted it was not true—thereupon said: "What phrasing do you wish to make?
translations.idiomatic: " Unconvinced, Huan snapped, "Supply the line now."

sentences.zh: 」宏即答云：「風鑒散朗，或搜或引，身雖可亡，道不可隕，宣城之節，信義為允也。

translations.literal: " Hong immediately replied saying: "Wind mirror scattered bright—sometimes gathering sometimes drawing—though body may perish, the Way cannot fall—integrity of Xuancheng—faith and righteousness as harmony.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuan improvised: "Far-sighted and forthright, now recruiting now guiding—life may end yet principle endures; Xuancheng's steadfast honor rings true as justice."

sentences.zh: 」溫泫然而止。

translations.literal: " Wen wept and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " Huan's eyes filled; he said no more.

sentences.zh: 宏賦又不及陶侃，侃子胡奴嘗于曲室抽刃問宏曰：「家君勳跡如此，君賦云何相忽？

translations.literal: Hong's fu also did not reach Tao Kan; Kan's son Hunu once in a secluded chamber drew blade and asked Hong saying: "My lord father's merit traces are thus—why does your fu so neglect him?
translations.idiomatic: The rhapsody also snubbed Tao Kan—whose son Hunu cornered Yuan in a side room with a knife: "My father's deeds tower—why erase him?"

sentences.zh: 」宏窘急，答曰：「我已盛述尊公，何乃言無？

translations.literal: " Hong embarrassed and hurried replied saying: "I have already greatly narrated your honored father—how then say there is none?
translations.idiomatic: " Flustered, Yuan protested, "I praised him lavishly—how can you say he is missing?"

sentences.zh: 」因曰：「精金百汰，在割能斷，功以濟時，職思靜亂，長沙之勳，為史所贊。

translations.literal: " Thereupon said: "Refined gold hundred washings—in cutting able to sever—merit thereby aids the age—office thinks quelling chaos—merit of Changsha—is praised by historians.
translations.idiomatic: " He extemporized: "Metal refined through countless heats cuts clean—his service steadied the age and stilled rebellion; historians hymn the Duke of Changsha's feats."

sentences.zh: 」胡奴乃止。

translations.literal: " Hunu thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " Hunu lowered the blade.

sentences.zh: 後為《三國名臣頌》曰：

translations.literal: Later he composed "Eulogies on Famous Ministers of the Three Kingdoms," saying:
translations.idiomatic: He later compiled "Eulogies for Three Kingdoms Ministers," opening:

sentences.zh: 從桓溫北征，作《北征賦》，皆其文之高者。

translations.literal: Following Huan Wen on northern expedition he composed the "Northern Expedition Fu"—both are among the heights of his writings.
translations.idiomatic: His northern campaign with Huan Wen produced the "Northern Expedition Rhapsody"—among his loftiest pieces.

sentences.zh: 嘗與王珣、伏滔同在溫坐，溫令滔讀其《北征賦》，至「聞所傳于相傳，雲獲麟於此野，誕靈物以瑞德，奚授體于虞者！

translations.literal: Once together with Wang Xun and Fu Tao they sat in Wen's presence; Wen ordered Tao to read his "Northern Expedition Fu," reaching "I hear what is transmitted from transmission—clouds caught the unicorn in this wilderness—birth spiritual thing by auspicious virtue—why grant body to the Yu ruler!
translations.idiomatic: Once Wang Xun, Fu Tao, and Yuan joined Huan Wen; Huan had Fu read the "Northern Expedition" aloud until the passage: "Tradition upon tradition tells how the unicorn was taken in this field—the spirit beast appeared as an omen of virtue—why should Heaven lend its form to the house of Yu?"

sentences.zh: 疚尼父之洞泣，似實慟而非假。

translations.literal: Affliction for Ni Father's deep weeping—seems truly grief and not false.
